newsitem.title: USA: Nextel launches combination phone service.
newsitem.headline: Nextel launches combination phone service.

text.p: Nextel Communications Inc on Monday launched a digital, wireless communications service which consolidates cellular, paging and instant conferencing into one phone.

The service is initially available in the Chicago and Milwaukee areas and northern Indiana, and other markets are expected to open later this year. The service is targeted toward busineses and is expected to expand into the consumer market, Nextel said.

The technology behind the service is known as iDEN (integrated digital enhanced network) and was developed by Motorola Inc. In June, Nextel placed an order with Motorola valued at more than $100 million.
In addition to offering combined cellular, paging and two-way radio, the technology is said to improve cellular call quality and decrease the number of disconnected calls.
Nextel is offering an 8.7 ounce phone for the service, called the iP370 PowerFone. It is manufactured by Motorola and sells between $369 and $429, the company said.
The basic service package is priced at $30 a month including 250 minutes of instant conferencing and 50 paging messages. Cellular calls will be billed at per minute rates.
